title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten specific campus spaces whose practical student uses are documented by Butler offices, libraries, and campus resources.

cards.title: Store Lunch, Then Stay Awhile
cards.subtitle: Atherton Union 011
cards.notes: Use the lockers, refrigerator, microwave, tables, and soft seating; ask about key and access procedures first.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built base for commuter students between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler lists lockers, food-storage appliances, study tables, whiteboards, soft seating, and a television in the center.
cards.access_notes: Intended for Butler commuter students; verify building access and current room scheduling.

cards.title: Draft in Jordan 304A
cards.subtitle: Jordan Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Bring a draft and use the room as a writing-focused stop; observe posted class or program restrictions.
cards.short_summary: A named writing space with basic break amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler’s commuter resource page identifies the Writer’s Studio in Jordan Hall 304A and notes a coffee maker and refrigerator.
cards.access_notes: Campus community access is subject to Jordan Hall hours and any posted room use.

cards.title: Practice in Room 319
cards.subtitle: Jordan Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Use this named center for language-related work and yield whenever a scheduled class or program needs the room.
cards.short_summary: A subject-specific place for language study in Jordan Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler lists the Modern Language Center, Jordan Hall Room 319, among commuter lounges and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use depends on Jordan Hall hours and posted academic scheduling.

cards.title: Find the Basement Seating
cards.subtitle: Gallahue Hall
cards.notes: Use available seating between science classes and keep corridors, doors, and scheduled teaching areas clear.
cards.short_summary: An officially listed soft-space option in the science complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler’s commuter resources identify the Gallahue Hall basement as a soft space in an academic building.
cards.access_notes: Available during applicable building hours; respect academic and laboratory access controls.

cards.title: Work Between Media Classes
cards.subtitle: Fairbanks Center, first and second floors
cards.notes: Choose an open seat on either listed floor, keep production routes clear, and relocate for scheduled activity.
cards.short_summary: Two floors of officially identified informal work space.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler identifies the first and second floors of Fairbanks as soft spaces commuters can use to study or hang out.
cards.access_notes: Use during building hours and follow any room-specific signs or production restrictions.

cards.entity_name: Pharmacy and Health Sciences Building Basement
cards.title: Bring a Problem Set Downstairs
cards.subtitle: Pharmacy and Health Sciences Building
cards.notes: Use the open seating and whiteboards for coursework; bring markers and avoid restricted teaching or lab areas.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level work zone with writable surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler lists basement seating, open spaces, and whiteboards in the Pharmacy and Health Sciences Building.
cards.access_notes: Academic-building access only; laboratories and controlled areas are not included.

cards.title: Meet Inside the Union
cards.subtitle: Atherton Union
cards.notes: Use the named student space for an informal meetup and check event postings before settling in with a group.
cards.short_summary: A designated student gathering area within Atherton Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler lists Dawg Den among Atherton Union’s event, meeting, and study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Subject to Atherton Union hours, events, and university policies.

cards.title: Connect in Atherton 004
cards.subtitle: Atherton Union garden level
cards.notes: Visit to learn about its offices and student organizations; respect programs that specify a particular audience.
cards.short_summary: A shared home for DEI staff and multiple student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler identifies the Efroymson Diversity Center in Atherton 004 and lists several student organizations housed there.
cards.access_notes: Campus-community space; activities may have registration or audience requirements.

cards.title: Pause Across from Schrott
cards.subtitle: Blue house across from Schrott Center
cards.notes: Check the current program calendar, enter respectfully, and use the center for reflection or community connection.
cards.short_summary: A named campus center for religious, spiritual, and meaning-making communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Butler’s orientation schedule locates the Compass Center across from Schrott and describes programming with campus ministries.
cards.access_notes: Check program hours and whether a particular gathering requires registration.

cards.title: Take the Call in a Booth
cards.subtitle: Irwin Library entrance and third floor
cards.notes: Use a privacy booth for a call that needs separation, then return it promptly for the next library patron.
cards.short_summary: Two defined library booths for private phone conversations.
cards.evidence_claim: Irwin Library documents two privacy booths: one near the entrance and one outside Information Technology on the third floor.
cards.access_notes: Available during library access hours; follow posted use limits and library conduct rules.
